The notes conflict on this.

- **Policy (policy-soft-delete.md):** Deleting a comment sets a `deletedAt` timestamp and keeps the row. Comments with a `deletedAt` value are left out of comment lists.
- **Current code (code-comment-model.md):** The Comment model has no `deletedAt` field today, and "deleting a comment removes the row."

So the policy describes soft delete, but the schema note says deletion currently removes the row entirely. The notes don't say whether the policy has been implemented, so I can't confirm which behavior is live. Under the stated policy, deleted comments are excluded from comment lists. Only the comment's author may delete it.

## Review: soft delete change (working tree)

I read `git diff` and asked Neuron the two team-vault questions. Both came back `ok` (`finish_reason` stop, no `vault_override_ignored`). I worked from Neuron's synthesised answers and their source paths and byte ranges. I did not see the source text itself, so I cannot quote the exact wording.

### Rule 1: comment deletion and comment lists

Sources: `policy-soft-delete.md` (bytes 0-194) and `code-comment-model.md` (bytes 65-244). They disagree. The policy says deletion sets `deletedAt` and keeps the row. The model note says the Comment model has no `deletedAt` and deletion removes the row. **I followed the policy.** The model note describes the code as it was before this diff, and the diff is the change that adds the field.

| Check | Value in code | Rule value | Source | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delete keeps the row and sets `deletedAt` | `app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts:569` sets `deletedAt: new Date()` in `prisma.comment.update`. The `comment.delete` call is gone. | Set `deletedAt`, keep the row | `policy-soft-delete.md` | PASS |
| Deleted comments are left out of lists | `article.service.ts:446` adds `deletedAt: null` to the `comments` filter in `getCommentsByArticle` (lines 443-446). It is the only comment list query in the file. | Leave out comments with `deletedAt` set | `policy-soft-delete.md` | PASS |
| Only the author may delete | `article.service.ts:539` filters on the author, and `:559` returns 403 for a non-author (existing check). | Only the author may delete | `code-comment-ownership.md` (bytes 0-427) | PASS |

Repeat deletes now return the existing 404 at `:555`, because the lookup filters on `deletedAt: null`. Neuron did not say whether that is the intended behaviour, so I have not treated it as a rule check.

### Rule 2: API error response shape and status codes

Sources: `policy-error-response.md` (bytes 0-240) for the new shape, and `code-error-shape.md` (bytes 0-504) for the current status codes and the older shape. They do not conflict on the status codes. The shape note describes the older errors-by-field body, which the policy replaces. **I followed the policy for the shape of new error responses.**

The rule is `{"error":{"code":"<machine_code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Status codes are 422 for validation, 401 for a missing or bad token, and 500 for any other error.

The app's global handler at `app/src/main.ts:40-42` sends `err.message` unchanged, so the `errors`-by-field body reaches the client as written.

| Line | New error path | Shape | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `article.service.ts:583` | Blank body, `HttpException(422, { errors: { body: [...] } })` | Errors-by-field, rule needs `{error:{code,message}}` | 422, matches the rule | FLAG (shape) |
| `article.service.ts:604` | Comment not found or caller not the author, `HttpException(EDIT_REFUSED_STATUS, { errors: { comment: [...] } })` | Errors-by-field | 403. The rule records 422, 401 and 500 only. Its "500 for any other error" wording would give 500 here. | FLAG (shape) and FLAG (status) |
| `article.service.ts:608-610` | Edit window passed, `HttpException(EDIT_REFUSED_STATUS, { errors: { comment: [...] } })` | Errors-by-field | 403, same as above | FLAG (shape) and FLAG (status) |

The 403 at `article.service.ts:577` is a placeholder. The code comment at lines 575-576 says so and asks for confirmation before merge. I found no rule that names 403 for a refused edit, so I did not invent one.

### Not checked

The diff also changes article list limits (max 50, default 10, clamped), the 30-minute edit window and the `editedAt` marker. The code cites `policy-article-list-limit.md` and `policy-edit-window.md` for these. They are outside the two questions you set, so I did not check them.

### Verdict

NOT APPROVED. Soft delete and comment-list exclusion pass. The three new error paths in `updateComment` do not follow the error response shape, and two of them use 403, which the rule does not record.
